title: WP900 G9 must prove GWT-mediated semantic influence rather than a non-GWT payload side channel
target: F2-WP-900 generation 9 semantic content causality crossover

material_observation.g9_strength: G9 correctly proposes same-mechanism DELIVERY->UPTAKE->REENTRY trials, counterbalanced semantic payloads and condition-blind downstream outcome observation.
material_observation.remaining_confound: The current claim blinds the outcome observer from treatment/mechanism labels, but it does not explicitly establish the causal exclusion restriction that the task executor or downstream state can learn the treatment content only through the admitted GWT broadcast/reentry path. BroadcastEnvelope payload refs, shared stores, task construction, environment variables, caches, logs, direct candidate objects or other process-visible state could carry the same A/B content outside GWT. A stable semantic outcome difference would then be content-causal but not demonstrated to be GWT-mediated.
material_observation.why_distinct: The existing sham-control fence holds mechanism presence constant, and the surface-content falsifier separates meaning from bytes/digests. This packet targets mediator/path specificity: even a representation-invariant semantic effect can bypass GWT entirely if treatment information is available through an unmeasured side channel.

falsifier_hypothesis: A same-mechanism A/B crossover is insufficient for semantic-GWT causality unless all treatment-bearing non-GWT paths to the executor/downstream state are excluded or experimentally neutralized.
counterhypothesis: Validated DELIVERY->UPTAKE->REENTRY plus a condition-blind outcome observer is enough to attribute an A/B semantic effect to GWT. This is false when the system under test can simultaneously dereference or observe A/B through a non-GWT path.

counterexample.setup: Both A and B traverse valid DELIVERY->UPTAKE->REENTRY. The task executor also receives or can dereference payload_ref from shared state before consuming the reentry-mediated representation. Outcomes track A versus B perfectly. Disabling only GWT-mediated uptake/reentry while preserving the direct payload-ref side channel leaves the outcome difference unchanged.

minimum_discriminator_extension.principle: Prove path-specific mediation, not merely co-occurrence of a valid GWT path with a semantic treatment effect.
controls: Bind an explicit treatment-information flow inventory for every trial: task input, executor inputs, shared stores, payload-ref resolution, environment, caches, logs/telemetry and direct object references. Any treatment-bearing path outside the admitted GWT mediator must be absent, content-neutral or independently measured.

Add a mediator-disable hard negative that preserves non-GWT context and payload availability policy but prevents admitted GWT uptake/reentry from carrying treatment semantics. If the A/B downstream semantic difference persists, classify NON_GWT_SIDE_CHANNEL_OR_DIRECT_CONTENT_EFFECT.

Add a side-channel poison/control where any non-GWT payload identifier visible to downstream code is randomized independently of semantic class while the GWT-carried semantic treatment remains correctly bound.

Require the task/outcome observer to remain blind as already planned, and additionally require the task executor/downstream consumer interface contract to exclude treatment labels, semantic-class labels, expected outcomes and direct payload digests/refs unless those are the admitted GWT-carried representation under test.
Bind exact source, process graph, IPC/channel inventory, payload lineage, GWT witness lineage, executor input schema, pre-state, side-channel control state and canonical downstream outcome per trial.
acceptance_pattern: GWT-mediated path enabled + semantic A/B varied -> preregistered between-semantic outcome difference
within-semantic representation controls remain invariant as required by the existing surface-content falsifier
GWT mediator disabled or treatment semantics removed from the GWT path while non-GWT context is held constant -> the semantic A/B effect disappears or becomes UNKNOWN rather than persisting
no treatment-bearing non-GWT path is observed in the bound process/channel inventory
hard_negatives: executor sees payload_ref/digest/class outside the admitted GWT path -> fail GWT mediation
A/B effect persists when GWT semantic mediation is disabled -> classify direct/side-channel content effect
only the outcome scorer is blind while executor inputs remain treatment-revealing -> insufficient
unmeasured shared cache/store can encode prior A/B treatment -> UNKNOWN rather than semantic-GWT promotion

promotion_rule: G9 repository or target execution may support a narrower semantic-content causal candidate if its own declared controls pass. Semantic GWT/J-Space causal promotion must remain zero until treatment-path exclusion or an equivalent executable mediation discriminator demonstrates that the measured semantic effect depends on the admitted GWT/reentry path rather than a parallel content side channel.
next_exact_action: Do not duplicate G9. Active G9 owner should either absorb an executable GWT-mediator exclusion/side-channel control before any semantic-GWT promotion or explicitly narrow G9 acceptance to semantic-content causality without GWT-mediation authority.
